commitResults.messageTitle: Rename package and main class for WhatsCooking
Add Recipe, RecipeList and Ingredient skeleton
commitResults.messageBody:
- Recipe: title, type, serving size, ingredients, steps, note, plus
  getters and add helpers.
- RecipeList: ArrayList<Recipe> wrapper with add() & get() functionality.
- Ingredient: thin stub wrapping one unparsed description string, to
  be extended later with quantity/name parsing.

- showWelcome/showGoodbye/readCommand: basic console I/O.
- showError/showMessage: consistent formatted output.
- showRecipe: show one recipe in full, by object or by 1-based index.
- listRecipes: show every recipe as a numbered summary.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Command hierarchy, Parser, and command stubs
commitResults.messageBody:
- Command: abstract base with execute(RecipeList, Ui) and isExit().
- ExitCommand: ends the app on "bye" or "exit".
- Parser: splits input into a command word + arguments, and maps the
  word to a Command via a switch statement.
- AddCommand/RetrieveCommand/SearchCommand: minimal stubs (constructor
  + a "not yet implemented" execute()) for Persons B/C/D to fill in,
  already wired into Parser's switch.
Each command is its own subclass rather than one class branching on
the command word, so implementing add/retrieve/search means editing a
dedicated file instead of a shared method.

commitResults.messageTitle: Wire up the main loop and add skeleton tests
commitResults.messageBody:
WhatsCooking.main() now runs the real loop: read a line via Ui, parse
it into a Command via Parser, execute it against a shared RecipeList,
repeat until isExit(). Every WhatsCookingException is caught in one
place, so a bad command shows an error and the loop continues instead
of crashing.
Adds RecipeListTest (bounds-checking) and ParserTest (dispatch to
ExitCommand, rejection of unknown commands) as a template for Persons
B/C/D's own command tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Standardise command error handling on exceptions
commitResults.messageBody:
AddCommand reported invalid titles, ingredients and steps via
ui.showError() and returned, while every other command throws
WhatsCookingException and lets the main loop display the error. Convert
those three paths to throw instead, so error detection and error display
stay separated and all commands report failures the same way.

Update AddCommandTest and AddCommandIngredientTest accordingly; the
invalid-input cases now assert that execute() throws as well as leaving
the recipe list unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add central logging setup and log the main loop
commitResults.messageBody:
Java logs to the console at INFO by default, which would interleave
diagnostics with the recipe output the user is reading. AppLogger
detaches the console handlers and writes to whatscooking.log instead,
which .gitignore now excludes along with the personal CLAUDE.local.md.
WhatsCooking logs start, exit, and errors shown to the user.

- Blank input now reports that no command was entered

- Private constructor for Parser, fix ExitCommand Javadoc and import order

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover Recipe and ExitCommand, and widen Parser tests - Add RecipeTest and ExitCommandTest, which had no tests - ParserTest 2 to 6 cases: exit, each subclass, blank input - Drop the template's sampleTest

Add a view command to list all recipes Ui.listRecipes() existed but no command called it, so there was no way to see recipes already added without knowing their number or name. ViewCommand wires it up, showing each recipe's name, type and servings.
Add tests for ViewCommand - ViewCommandTest: viewing leaves the recipe list unchanged, empty or not - ParserTest: add a view case to the existing dispatch test
